text:
Sam: quick Q — for per-route quotas + burst smoothing, what's the canonical 429 contract we want to ship? specifically: streaming vs non-streaming, embeddings vs chat, and header names (Retry-After only or extra X-RateLimit-* headers)?
Maria: i'd vote for Retry-After (widely supported) + a small set of X-RateLimit-* headers for tooling (Limit, Remaining, Reset). keep them optional so clients can fallback to Retry-After.
Tyler: agree. also: backward-compat rule — if we change header names, we keep the old ones for one release and document deprecation. no silent renames.
Priya: streaming edgecase: if quota hits mid-stream, how should client know? do we cut the socket, send final error chunk, or set a trailing header?
Sam: my take — for streaming we should send a final metadata chunk (json) and then close. e.g. last chunk: `{"type":"error","error":{"code":"rate_limit","message":"quota exceeded"}}` and include the Retry-After in the final headers/metadata. closing without message is too ambiguous.
Maria: +1 to final error chunk. also include X-RateLimit-Reset unix ts so robust clients can compute exact wait instead of guessing from Retry-After.
Tyler: small concern: X-RateLimit-Reset leaks server-side clock but that's fine; clients already use Retry-After. important: differentiate per-key vs per-route quotas in headers without exposing PII. maybe `X-RateLimit-Scope: project` or `route` instead of user ids.
Priya: example 429 headers proposal (for non-streaming):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-RateLimit-Limit: 900
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1774567902
X-RateLimit-Scope: project:embeddings
X-Quota-Used: 600
```
And body: `{"error":"quota_exceeded","code":"rate_limit","message":"per-route quota exceeded (embeddings-per-minute)"}`
Sam: client pseudo-code for retry logic we can recommend in SDKs:
```
if resp.status == 429:
  wait = parse_retry_after(resp.headers) or max(1, resp.headers['X-RateLimit-Reset'] - now)
  sleep(wait + jitter())
  retry_with_backoff()
```
Maria: also callout: streaming clients should parse a final error chunk and not immediately retry unless Retry-After present. two cases: short bursts (Retry-After small) vs long quota windows (use Reset).
Tyler: question — when capacity tiers fallback (dedicated -> hosted) do we return 503 or 429? current behavior sometimes returns 503 on capacity failover which confuses clients. we should standardize: use 429 for quota/limit hits, 503 for infra/capacity errors.
Priya: yes separate semantics. 429 = client-level throttling; 503 = server-side outage or capacity failover. add docs + tests.
Sam: who's taking API contract doc + tests? i'll open a PR to api-contracts with examples and a small suite that asserts headers for streaming/non-streaming. tagging @Maria @Tyler for review.
Maria: i'll review. can we include a migration note: clients should prefer Retry-After if present, else look for X-RateLimit-Reset. add examples for curl and SDKs.
Tyler: i'll add the canary rollout checklist: 1) feature flag, 2) emit both old+new headers, 3) telemetry for 429s by route, 4) monitor client error spikes.
rate-limiter-bot: dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/quotas?route=embeddings (shows current per-route windows and recent 429 spikes) :bar_chart:
Priya: sounds good. leaving small TODO: decide exact header names (underscores vs hyphens?) i prefer hyphens to match common practice.
Sam: great. i'll draft PR by EOD with concrete header names, streaming final-chunk example, and the client retry snippet. thanks all :thumbsup:
